title: Orbital-resolved superexchange and topological magnon bands in MXene Fe$_2$C
authors: Qiang Gao, Wei Wang, Shaojin Qi, Guimei Shi, Anbang Guo, Xin Jin, Chen Shen, Xing-Qiu Chen
abstract: Magnetic MXenes are promising candidates for future spintronics due to their intriguing properties. Nevertheless, the topological properties of magnon bands and superexchange mechanism remain relatively underexplored. In this work, we have calculated the spin wave dispersions for MXene Fe$_2$C using the linear spin wave method, with the exchange coupling parameters obtained from first-principles calculations. Owing to the staggered stacking of two Fe sub-lattices, the interlayer exchange coupling lifts the degeneracy of the ferromagnetic magnon modes. A Dirac point is identified in the magnon bands at the $K$ point. The topological properties of magnon bands, including Berry curvature, valley Chern number and edge states, are further computed by means of a two-band model. We also derive an effective Hamiltonian to explain the magnonic topology, which is protected by the $C_{3v}$ rotational symmetry. To understand the microscopic origin of the exchange couplings that govern the magnon bands, we then construct a refined model integrating perturbation theory and the tight-binding approach. The ferromagnetic superexchange coupling is mediated by the virtual hopping between the d orbitals of two distinct Fe sites via a pair of orthogonal p orbitals at the bridging C site. In detail, the intralayer exchange coupling is governed by the in-plane $p_x$ and $p_y$ orbitals, while the out-of-plane $p_z$ orbital is responsible for the interlayer exchange coupling. Our results establish a direct link between the orbital-resolved anisotropic superexchange and topological properties of the magnon bands in magnetic MXene Fe$_2$C, providing theoretical guidance for future spintronics applications.
summary: This theoretical study investigates the magnetic excitations and topological properties of MXene Fe2C. It successfully links the microscopic superexchange mechanism, detailing how orbital overlaps govern the exchange coupling, to the macroscopic topological features of the magnon bands. This provides crucial theoretical guidance for designing next-generation spintronic materials.
main_problem: The study aims to investigate the topological properties of magnon bands and the orbital-resolved superexchange mechanism in magnetic MXene Fe2C.
main_result: The research establishes a direct link between the orbital-resolved anisotropic superexchange and the topological properties of magnon bands, identifying a Dirac point at the K point.
method: The authors employed the linear spin wave method, combined with first-principles calculations and a two-band model, to analyze the magnetic excitations and topology.
model_or_system: The physical system is the magnetic MXene Fe2C. The analysis models the magnetic interactions using a Heisenberg Hamiltonian, incorporating intralayer and interlayer exchange couplings derived from orbital-resolved superexchange paths.
key_observables: Spin wave dispersions, Berry curvature, valley Chern number, edge states, and the orbital-resolved anisotropic superexchange coupling.
important_parameters: The interlayer exchange coupling is found to be stronger than the intralayer coupling, and the topology is protected by the C3v rotational symmetry.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the linear spin wave approximation and utilizes a two-band model for topological calculations.

paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first calculating spin wave dispersions using LSWT, then analyzing the topology via a two-band model, and finally deriving a refined model using perturbation theory and tight-binding to microscopically explain the orbital-resolved superexchange mechanism.
why_interesting: The connection between orbital physics (superexchange) and topological band theory in a 2D magnetic material is highly relevant for understanding emergent quantum phenomena in condensed matter systems.
